content_voiceover: This slide covers autologous stem cell transplant and the consolidation that can follow it. For the conditioning regimen going into autologous transplant, high dose melphalan remains the standard, typically dosed at one forty to two hundred milligrams per square meter of body surface area. Tandem autologous transplant, meaning a planned second transplant within six months of the first, isn't for everyone. Current evidence suggests it benefits two groups in particular, patients who fail to reach at least a very good partial response, or VGPR, within three months of their first transplant, and patients who present with high risk cytogenetics at diagnosis. In both groups, tandem transplant appears to improve both response depth and overall survival, though case selection really matters here. Moving to consolidation after autologous transplant, the general approach is to give two to four additional cycles using a regimen similar to what the patient received during induction. This is recommended specifically for patients who still haven't achieved a VGPR after transplant. Timing matters too, consolidation should ideally start within one to two months after transplant, and should not be delayed beyond three months.
keypoints: Standard conditioning is high dose melphalan at 140 to 200 mg per m squared
Tandem autologous transplant benefits patients without VGPR by 3 months post-transplant
High-risk cytogenetics at diagnosis also favors tandem transplant
Consolidation gives 2 to 4 cycles similar to induction if VGPR not reached
Start consolidation within 1 to 2 months, no later than 3 months post-transplant
keypoint_voiceover: To recap, high dose melphalan is the conditioning backbone for autologous transplant, and tandem transplant is reserved for patients without VGPR at three months or those with high risk cytogenetics. Consolidation, when used, mirrors the induction regimen for two to four cycles and should start within one to two months, no later than three months after transplant.
